requirement_text: For entry to all degrees, 6 subjects including English, Irish (unless exempt), and four other subjects in the Leaving Certificate (or equivalent GCE/GCSE or other acceptable qualification) are required.

requirement_text: Candidates born and fully educated outside the Republic of Ireland (26 counties) who are presenting qualifications other than the Leaving Certificate are automatically exempt from Irish. A third language must be included among subjects for most degree programmes in Arts, Human Sciences, Law, Social Science, Commerce, Medicine, and Health Sciences. Business programmes must include Mathematics. Science-family programmes (Science, Agriculture, Engineering, Food Science, Medicine, Dentistry, Health Sciences) must include Mathematics and a Science subject.
source_authority_note: ucc.ie is the official University College Cork domain but does not match the narrow .edu/.ac./.gov authority-gate pattern used by lib/acquisition/source-authority.ts.
limitations: Extraction step merged several distinct statements from the source page into one paraphrase; re-read the live page before ingesting as verbatim, and note the third-language/Mathematics/Science rules are college-level generalisations that individual programmes may vary.

requirement_text: Minimum grade H4 in two subjects and minimum grade O6/H7 in four other subjects, in the same sitting: English O6/H7, Irish O6/H7 (unless exempt), Mathematics O6/H7, another language O6/H7, Chemistry H4, and Physics or Biology H4. Applicants cannot combine results achieved in different sittings of the Leaving Certificate (or equivalent) for the purpose of meeting the minimum entry requirements.
source_authority_note: ucc.ie is the official University College Cork domain but does not match the narrow .edu/.ac./.gov authority-gate pattern used by lib/acquisition/source-authority.ts.
limitations: The single-sitting rule is stated specifically on the Medicine (CK701) page and recorded here as Medicine-specific; the general Ireland CAO-system research separately confirms domestic students can ordinarily combine Leaving Certificate matriculation subjects (not points) across sittings for most other courses, so this stricter single-sitting rule should not be generalised beyond Medicine without separate confirmation.
researcher_notes: Future change confirmed on this same page: from 2027 entry, 'Leaving Certificate scores above 550 points will no longer be moderated' and HPAT weighting reduces from a maximum of 300 to a maximum of 150 -- consistent with the national HPAT/points rebalancing found in the parallel CAO-system research.

requirement_text: Students are also required to present for the Admissions Test (HPAT-Ireland), which must be completed in the proposed year of entry to the Medicine programme.
source_authority_note: ucc.ie is the official University College Cork domain but does not match the narrow .edu/.ac./.gov authority-gate pattern used by lib/acquisition/source-authority.ts.
researcher_notes: UCC is one of the 6 Irish medical schools requiring HPAT-Ireland nationally, per the parallel CAO-system research.

requirement_text: Undergraduate minimums (varies by college): Arts/Business/Science -- IELTS 6.5 overall, 6.0 in each band; TOEFL iBT 90 overall, min 20 in each section (pre-21-Jan-2026 scale) or 4.5 overall (new scale, exams on/after 21 Jan 2026); Duolingo DET 120, min 110 in each section; PTE 63, min 59 per item. Medicine and Health -- IELTS 6.5 overall and 6.5 in each band; TOEFL iBT 90 (L23/R21/S22/W23); Duolingo 120 with min 120 in each section; PTE 63 with min 63 per item. Speech & Language Therapy (highest band) -- IELTS 7.0 overall, 6.5 in each band; TOEFL iBT 100; Duolingo 130 with min 120 in each section; PTE 72. English language tests must be undertaken no more than two years prior to commencement of a programme, and UCC will not accept a combination of individual component scores from multiple tests.
source_authority_note: ucc.ie is the official University College Cork domain but does not match the narrow .edu/.ac./.gov authority-gate pattern used by lib/acquisition/source-authority.ts.
limitations: For non-EU applicants specifically to the College of Medicine and Health, a separate UCC page states only IELTS, TOEFL, Duolingo, Cambridge, and Pearson PTE are accepted (a narrower list than for other colleges) -- not independently re-verified against this specific table in this pass.
researcher_notes: The post-21-Jan-2026 TOEFL rescale (e.g. '4.5 overall' for standard programmes) is cross-confirmed independently on Maynooth's and Galway's own English-requirement pages, so treated as a genuine industry-wide TOEFL iBT scoring change rather than an extraction artifact.

requirement_text: If your status is Non-EU, you should apply directly to the International Office using the undergraduate online application system, not through the CAO. Applicants submit directly to the International Office via the online system, with permission to apply for up to 2 programmes. Processing is approximately 3-5 weeks from receipt of a completed application. The application fee is €50. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and places are given on a first-come, first-served basis.
source_authority_note: ucc.ie is the official University College Cork domain but does not match the narrow .edu/.ac./.gov authority-gate pattern used by lib/acquisition/source-authority.ts.
researcher_notes: To determine EU vs non-EU fee/process status in the first place, UCC requires completing an 'EU/Non-EU Fees Assessment Form' submitted to feesassessments@ucc.ie, per a separate UCC page (ucc.ie/en/international/studyatucc/undergraduateprogrammes/euornoneuundergraduate/).

requirement_text: Non-EU applicants may enter Year 4 of the BSc (Hons) Architecture programme if they hold transcripts showing completion of 180 ECTS credits in accredited Architecture, achieved a minimum 50% overall average mark, and possess accredited programme credentials recognised for architectural-profession entry. Required documents include official transcripts, proof of identity, module descriptions, English language proficiency evidence (if applicable), and a design portfolio (maximum 20 pages, 5MB). The application process is usually open between December and June.
